questions.stem_en: Many teams create CloudWatch Logs log groups whose names start with /app/. Most of these log groups were created with the default retention, and storage costs keep growing. The company wants every existing and future log group with the /app/ prefix to keep log events for 90 days, without relying on each team to configure it. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Create an account-level retention policy for the /app/ prefix with a 90-day retention period and the NEW_ONLY option.
Create an account-level retention policy for the /app/ prefix with a 90-day retention period and the RETROACTIVE option.
Schedule an AWS Lambda function that lists the /app/ log groups every day and sets a 90-day retention on each one.
Ask each team to set a 90-day retention on its log groups, and review the settings every month.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch Logs の既定ではログデータは無期限に保存されます。アカウントレベルの保持ポリシーはロググループの設定より優先され、RETROACTIVE を指定すると、ポリシーを作る前からあるものも含めて接頭辞に合うすべてのロググループに適用されます。

per_choice.A: NEW_ONLY はポリシーを作った後に作られるロググループにだけ適用され、既存のロググループは無期限のままです。
per_choice.B: 正しい。既存と今後の /app/ のロググループのすべてに、チームの設定に頼らず 90 日の保持が適用されます。
per_choice.C: 動きますが、独自の関数を作って保守する必要があります。
per_choice.D: 各チームに頼ることになり、要件に反します。確認の手間もかかります。

references.quote: By default, log data is stored in CloudWatch Logs indefinitely.
Specify RETROACTIVE to apply the policy to every log group that matches the prefix, including log groups that existed before you created the policy.
Specify NEW_ONLY to apply the policy only to log groups that are created after you create the policy.
An account-level retention policy overrides the retention setting of the log group.

questions.stem_en: A company exports application logs to an Amazon S3 bucket as millions of small files of about 20 KB each. The team added an S3 Lifecycle rule that transitions objects to a lower-cost storage class after 30 days, but the objects stay in their original storage class and storage costs do not go down. What is the MOST likely reason?

choices_en.text: Lifecycle rules apply only to objects that are added after the rule is created, so the existing objects are not transitioned.
The bucket policy denies all actions for all principals, which prevents the lifecycle rule from transitioning the objects.
By default, S3 Lifecycle does not transition objects smaller than 128 KB to any storage class.
Lifecycle transitions are charged as data retrieval, so S3 skips transitions that would cost more than they save.

explanation.summary: S3 ライフサイクルは既定で、128 KB より小さいオブジェクトをどのストレージクラスへも移しません。小さなオブジェクトはオブジェクトごとに移行のリクエストの料金がかかり、節約より費用が大きくなることがあるため、移行は勧められていません。

per_choice.A: ライフサイクルのルールは既存のオブジェクトにも、後から足すオブジェクトにも適用されます。
per_choice.B: バケットポリシーでライフサイクルのルールによる削除や移行を止めることはできません。
per_choice.C: 正しい。約 20 KB のオブジェクトは既定の動きで移されません。
per_choice.D: ライフサイクルの移行にデータの取り出しの料金はかかりません。

references.quote: Amazon S3 applies a default behavior to S3 Lifecycle configurations that prevents objects smaller than 128 KB from being transitioned to any storage class.
When you add a Lifecycle configuration to a bucket, the configuration rules apply to both existing objects and objects that you add later.
You can't use a bucket policy to prevent deletions or transitions by an S3 Lifecycle rule.
There are no data retrieval charges for lifecycle transitions.
